statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 8 remains far below the block threshold, while stress rises to 71 in the high band as crude extends and the 10-year holds near its session high.
recommendation: Conditions remain consistent with normal mean-reverting behaviour: NQ sits mid-range after fading its session high, the consumer-credit beat passed without a directional impulse, and no repeated extension after failed retracements is observed. The narrow flagged window covers the remainder of the 19:00-20:00 UTC power hour and the 20:00 UTC closing auction, where rebalancing flow meets the widest sector dispersion of the session.
headline: NQ holds mid-range at 29,574 through the power hour as an $18.06B consumer-credit beat passes without impulse, while WTI +2.34% and a 4.806% 10-year keep stress in the high band
body: NQ futures trade near 29,574.00, up 0.03% on the session, inside a 29,425.00 to 29,764.75 day range. Price now sits 191 points below the session high and 149 points above the low, marginally under the range midpoint, having faded further over the past hour rather than extending from either extreme. That continued two-sided rotation is the direct opposite of the repeated-extension-after-failed-retracement structure that overwhelms this strategy, which is why tail is held at 8 despite firmer cross-asset channels. The cash index has drifted slightly lower: the Nasdaq-100 stands at 29,520.05, down 0.08%, inside a 29,400.70 to 29,655.73 range and now just under the 29,544.15 prior close, a drift of roughly 24 points rather than a directional leg. Volatility has ticked up from the day low without becoming disorderly, with VIX at 15.52, up 1.44%, mid-range within 15.22 to 15.94 and low in absolute terms. The scheduled Consumer Credit release for July printed during the 19:00 UTC hour and has been verified against the Federal Reserve G.19 statistical release: consumer credit increased at a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 4.2 percent, an $18.06 billion rise that took total outstanding credit to $5,186.2 billion and beat the $11.7 billion to $16.0 billion range of analyst estimates. A beat of that size on a second-tier household-credit series produced no observable directional impulse in index structure, which is the relevant fact for tail rather than the surprise magnitude itself. The rates channel is firmer and now sits at the top of its session range. The 10-year yield is at 4.806%, up about two basis points within a 4.760 to 4.812 range, and the 5-year is at 4.573%, up two basis points within 4.531 to 4.582. Yields printing at session highs into the close is a genuine stress amplifier, but it has not so far translated into one-way equity pressure. Index internals stay sharply split, which keeps the dominant mode at mixed rather than trend-up or trend-down. Semiconductors continue to lead on Qualcomm's multi-generational custom-silicon agreement with Amazon Web Services, which carries warrants over 25 million QCOM shares at $161.26 tied to up to $60 billion of purchase orders and lifted the stock more than 5%, while the Dow trades down around 1.1% and the S&P 500 around 0.5% lower. Rotation into a single-name silicon catalyst against broad cyclical weakness is dispersion, not index-level one-way pressure. The energy channel has firmed again since the prior assessment and is the main reason stress steps from 69 to 71. WTI near $93.62 is up 2.34% and Brent near $98.61 is up 1.50%, both at six-week highs after Saudi Arabia halted operations at several southern energy facilities following Houthi strikes on the 400,000 barrel-per-day Jazan refinery and other sites. The counterweight remains the reported Iran-Oman temporary Hormuz corridor, which Iran has previewed as days away, though transit management terms are unresolved. No new Middle East escalation has been reported in the past hour. Canada's retaliatory tariffs of up to 50% on about $20 billion of US goods took effect today and remain in force. Rate expectations are the third open channel, with Friday's strong payrolls report leaving September Federal Reserve hike odds broadly balanced ahead of Thursday's PPI and Friday's CPI and the 15-16 September FOMC. Shared Finviz cross-asset context was collected at 16:52 UTC and is now roughly 158 minutes old, past the 90-minute freshness limit, so it is treated as stale and is not relied upon; the independent live research above is the evidence base. The flagged window covers the remainder of the power hour and the 20:00 UTC closing auction, extended to 20:15 UTC to include immediate post-close repricing.

lookbackSummary: Across the last 24 hours the assessment stayed inside the EA_ON band without interruption. Tail ran between 5 and 10 from Monday evening through Tuesday morning, stepped up to 15 in the 14:00 UTC slot on an observed cash-open downside leg that left NQ near the session low, then fell back to 8, 7 and 6 as that leg was fully retraced. Stress climbed steadily from the low 60s during Monday's Labor Day holiday session to a peak of 72 in early Tuesday afternoon as crude extended on the Saudi facility strikes and Canada's retaliatory tariffs took effect, eased to the high 60s through the afternoon, and is now firming again as crude presses to six-week highs. The dominant mode was mixed for most of the window because cross-asset signals kept diverging from Nasdaq price action, sat at normal through the quiet Monday evening hours, and turned to trend-down only for the single hour that carried the decline. The 09:00 UTC slot has no published assessment and is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The horizon opens inside the power hour with NQ mid-range, the consumer-credit beat already absorbed without impulse, and conditional tail at 8. It steps up to the late-session peak of 10 at the 20:00 UTC cash close, where imbalance flow concentrates into the widest sector dispersion of the session; that hour closes the flagged window. Conditional tail then falls to the horizon floor of 5 through the Asian session, with the 07:00 UTC European open on 9 September and the 13:30 UTC US cash open as the next flow checkpoints. The first full hour after that open carries the horizon peak at 13, because opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks is the specific structure capable of overwhelming mean reversion. The horizon closes on the 17:00 UTC pairing of the Apple product event keynote and the US 10-Year Note Auction, which together lift the conditional score to 10. All 24 slots stay inside the EA_ON band. Three unresolved channels could force a step change in either direction: Middle East energy, where the halted Saudi operations still have no confirmed restart date while the reported Iran-Oman Hormuz corridor cuts the other way; the North American trade dispute after Canada's tariffs took effect; and rate expectations into Thursday's PPI and Friday's CPI ahead of the 15-16 September FOMC, with the 10-year now printing at its session high. Stress stays in the high band throughout because none of those channels resolves inside the horizon, while confidence decays overnight as the live evidence base ages and recovers once the 9 September cash session provides fresh observable structure.
